corpus: NASA mission mishap and failure investigation reports
purpose: Rights-clean multi-hop Graph RAG evaluation corpus. Documents were chosen because their stories interlock through shared contractors (Lockheed Martin), shared review-board members, a shared mishap-investigation procedure (NPD/NPG/NPR 8621.1), shared heritage hardware and shared root-cause themes.

extraction.page_marker: \f--- page N ---\n before each page's text; each page block ends with exactly one newline
extraction.encoding: utf-8, LF newlines, no normalisation, no OCR

rights_classes.us-gov-work: Authored by a NASA board / NASA organisation; a work of the US Government, no copyright asserted.
rights_classes.copyright-notice-present: The document itself carries a copyright notice.
rights_classes.gov-public-release: Official public-release investigation report. The repository never hosts or redistributes full PDFs; documents are fetched directly from official NASA/NTRS servers, with only brief test excerpts retained for evaluation.
rights_classes.unclear: No copyright notice in the document, but authorship or a distribution marking means public-domain status should not be assumed. Owner decides.

documents.text_quality: OCR of a scanned NTRS copy. Body prose is accurate (spot-checked p45 against the page image, word-for-word) but line breaks are aggressive (one phrase per line), table structure is lost, and the front-matter/TOC pages (pp3-8) are heavily garbled. 13 pages are figure-only with no text.

documents.title: NOAA N-PRIME Mishap Investigation Final Report
documents.authoring_org: NOAA N-PRIME Mishap Investigation Board, NASA (chair: Christopher Scolese, Deputy Associate Administrator for Space Science, NASA Headquarters)
documents.verbatim_notice: As requested on September 27, 2004, we have completed our review of the NOAA N Prime Mishap Report (Report) under NASA Procedural Requirements (NPR) 8621.1, "Procedural Requirements for Mishap Reporting, Investigating, and Recordkeeping." We also reviewed the endorsement pages from the Deputy Associate Administrator of the Science Mission Directorate and the Chief, Office of Safety and Mission Assurance. Based on our review, we recommend releasing the Report subject to the comments below. In an e-mail from Jeff Smith, Director, Civil Space West Coast Operations, Lockheed Martin, dated October 1, 2004, Lockheed Martin has identified several sections of the report which include information that they consider proprietary information. Also, the External Relations Office has identified information in the Report which is export controlled. Both the proprietary information and the export-controlled information should be redacted before release of the Report.
documents.rights_note: NASA-authored (NASA HQ letterhead cover, NASA MIB, endorsed by Bryan O'Connor, Chief OSMA). The verbatim notice above is the NASA Office of General Counsel release memorandum bound as page 2 of the PDF; it is the release authority for this public version, from which Lockheed Martin proprietary and export-controlled passages were redacted (the redactions are visible in the body as 'Proprietary Information' / 'Export Controlled' markers).
documents.text_quality: MIXED: pages 1-21 (cover, General Counsel letter, endorsements, OSMA critique, board roster images, TOC) are scanned images with NO text layer and are therefore empty in the .txt; pages 22-113 are native digital text and are clean. Not OCR'd, per instruction. The board roster IS recoverable because it is repeated as digital text on page 24.
